subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Ariane 5 Explosion: A Software Integer Overflow
description: Learn The Ariane 5 Explosion: A Software Integer Overflow in one minute.

hook.text: On June 4, 1996, the Ariane 5 rocket self-destructed 37 seconds after launch. The payload was worth $370 million.

buildup.text: The inertial navigation system converted a 64-bit floating point number to a 16-bit integer. The value was too large.

discovery.text: The overflow triggered an exception. Both redundant navigation computers crashed simultaneously — they ran identical code.

twist.text: The faulty code was reused from Ariane 4 without testing. Ariane 5 was faster, producing larger numbers the code couldn't handle.

climax.text: The ESA now mandates testing reused software in new contexts. Redundancy with identical code provides zero actual backup.

punchline.text: One number too big. Both computers crashed. $370 million gone.

quiz.question: Why did redundant computers fail to prevent the Ariane 5 crash?
options: The backup computer was powered by the same battery that failed
Both computers ran identical code, so the same bug crashed both simultaneously
The explosion destroyed the backup computer before it could take over
